blindComparison: No reference-title footage was supplied, so no measured side-by-side preference is claimed.
scope: Independent read-only review of the completed cb4 motion artifact: provenance, 300 rendered frames, screen-crossing black ribbons, character/cloth readability and combat feedback.

apparatus.limitation: 60 Hz is a virtual capture clock on SwiftShader; this is not physical-device performance.

clearedWithinScope: No large screen-crossing black ribbon was observed in all 300 thumbnails plus 11 native samples.
A real incoming enemy hit and a separate outgoing player hit are present.
Both MP4s contain unique consecutive rendered frames.

findings.shot: locomotion-walk-040; locomotion-run-100; combat-combat-setup-000; combat-enemy-startup-007; combat-enemy-active-025; combat-reaction-068
findings.problem: The player and ronin still read as primitive mannequins: oval heads, orange cylindrical joints, broad rectangular sleeve masses and flat skirt panels. Overlap makes arm and weapon ownership hard to read.
findings.why: E07 and E12 require a clear character, sword and attack-phase silhouette at speed and in shadow.
findings.hypothesis: Visible body/garment construction and insufficient material separation may both contribute; native pixels alone do not separate them.
findings.fix: Inspect the same six poses under a neutral diagnostic material, then improve layered clothing and arm-to-weapon readability within existing budgets. Require zero surviving readability majors in a new independent native review.
findings.evidence: All six named native PNGs; primary player region approximately x1000 y450 w330 h650.

findings.problem: The red full-screen edge flash appears at f109 when the player hits the enemy, and is absent at f68 when the enemy reduces player health.
findings.why: The strongest damage cue identifies the opposite event, so taking damage and landing a hit are visually confused.
findings.hypothesis: The player damage event is suppressed while the screen feedback consumer accepts an enemy damage event.
findings.fix: Make Combat emit exactly one player damage event and restrict the red lens to the damaged local player. Re-capture both directions and compare event frames with native before/after frames.
findings.evidence: Perimeter red-excess f67/f68/f69 = 16.73/16.32/16.66; f108/f109/f110 = 16.14/64.37/60.53. Health/event records identify f68 as incoming and f109 as outgoing.
